Synkopa 0.9.32 — usability review

21 findings from a full pass over the app’s main surfaces: first run, menus and settings, Channel rack, Piano roll, Playlist, Mixer and effects, browser, export and help. Each one shows the screenshot, what happens and why it hurts.

Build: main 65659c6 (Release 0.9.32)Reviewed: 23 November 2026Viewports: 1920 × 1080, 1366 × 768, 150% scaleCapture: UI mock build in headless Chromium
21findings
5High: data risk or core surface
9Medium: friction and mistakes
7Low: polish and consistency

Summary

Synkopa is coherent and unusually complete for its size: an FL-style keymap applied consistently, search, themes and an interface scale, and an effect picker that is better than what most DAWs ship. Nearly every control has a thoughtful tooltip, and the export, record and unsaved-changes flows give clear feedback. Nothing below needs a change of architecture; all of it is UI-layer work.

The high-severity issues fall into two groups. Silent, hard-to-undo actions from small targets or from another view: a right-click that deletes a clip, and a pattern edit that rewrites the arrangement. A Piano roll that is hard to read precisely: its ruler and its pitch grid both fail at the exact job they exist to do.

Fix these five first

  1. U1 Right-click deletes clips; the menu is a 12 × 15 px target
  2. U2 Changing a pattern’s length silently stretches and overlaps its clips
  3. U3 Piano roll ruler: three numbering schemes in the same style
  4. U4 Piano roll grid: pitch rows are almost invisible
  5. U5 Default type and hit targets are tiny at 100% scale

U1 High Playlist Reproduced

Right-click deletes a clip instantly; the clip menu is a 12 × 15 px target

What happens

In the Playlist a right-click on a clip deletes it at once, with no message. The context menu opens only from the clip’s top-left corner: a zone 12 px wide and 15 px tall, immediately to the right of the 8 px trim edge. Left- and right-click both open the menu there.

Why it is a problem

  • Right-click is the universal “show me the menu” gesture; Ableton, Logic, REAPER and Bitwig all open a context menu with it. FL Studio deletes too, so this is FL parity, but the target is tiny by any standard: at 100% scale it is 12 × 15 px, half the 24 × 24 px minimum WCAG 2.2 recommends for pointers, and the cost of missing by a few pixels is losing a clip.
  • While aiming for the menu, the reviewer deleted the clip 5 times out of 5 before hitting the zone once.
  • Nothing confirms the deletion or points to undo: no toast, the hint line and the status readout do not change.
  • The zone is not marked. The glyph in the corner reads as a “pattern” type icon, not as a menu handle.

Suggested direction

Keep the FL gesture, but (1) show a transient “Deleted 1 clip · Undo (Ctrl+Z)” toast, (2) widen the menu zone to the clip’s whole header strip so right-click on the header is “menu” and on the body is “delete”, and (3) mark the corner as a handle on hover.

Code: ui/src/views/Playlist.tsx:678, ui/src/views/Playlist.tsx:744

U2 High Playlist ↔ Channel rack Reproduced

Changing a pattern’s length silently stretches every clip of it in the Playlist

What happens

With two 1-bar clips of Pattern 1 placed in the Playlist, pressing “+ add a bar” in the Channel rack made the pattern 2 bars. Both clips instantly became 2 bars as well: the first (beats 1–9) now runs underneath the second (6.5–14.5). Clicking a step in the greyed bar beyond the pattern does the same. No message is shown.

Why it is a problem

  • An edit made in one view rewrites the arrangement in another, which may be covered by the Channel rack or hidden altogether.
  • Overlapping clips of the same pattern double-trigger notes and change what plays. The only cue is a hatch on the overlapped header.
  • Extending patterns (1 → 2 → 4 bars) while an arrangement grows is one of the most common moves in pattern-based production.
  • In clip-based DAWs (Ableton Live, Bitwig, REAPER) instances keep their own length when the source grows.

Suggested direction

Keep clip lengths by default and show a “pattern is longer than this clip” marker with a one-click fit, or make the resize an explicit, visible, undoable step (“2 clips resized to 2 bars · Undo”). Never let clips overlap silently.

Code: ui/src/views/ChannelRack.tsx:75, ops: follow_pattern_length (engine)

U3 High Piano roll Measured

Time ruler mixes three numbering schemes in the same style

What happens

Bar starts show a bare number (“1”), the other beats show “bar.beat” (“1.2”), and every 16th inside a beat shows a bare digit (“2”, “3”, “4”). All are 10 px monospace in three nearly identical greys, so the row reads “1 2 3 4 1.2 2 3 4 1.3 …”.

Why it is a problem

  • The digits after a bar number are 16th positions but look exactly like beat numbers. The reviewer, experienced with DAWs, clicked what looked like beats 2, 3 and 4 and got three consecutive 16ths.
  • The hierarchy is inverted: bar numbers (#8d96a3) are dimmer than beat labels (#98a1ae), and the 16th digits (#687282 on #191c23, 3.5:1) are hard to read at 10 px.
  • Every DAW ruler labels bars and beats and leaves subdivisions as tick marks.

Suggested direction

Bars bright and bold, beats smaller, 16ths as tick marks only (optionally “1.1.2” once a 16th is 48 px wide or more). Raise the digits to 11 px and at least 4.5:1.

Code: ui/src/ui/timeRuler.ts:26, ui/src/ui/timeRuler.ts:59

U4 High Piano roll Measured

Grid: pitch rows are almost indistinguishable

What happens

Sampled from the canvas: adjacent key rows differ by 1.01–1.06:1 and a black-key row differs from a white-key row by about 1.08:1. The 16th lines (#13161c on a #0f1115 background) are about 1.1:1.

Why it is a problem

  • With no readable row line, the only pitch cue is the 45 px key lane at the far left, away from the pointer.
  • Landing a note on the wrong semitone (E instead of F, B instead of C) is easy and silent.
  • FL Studio and Ableton both shade black-key rows clearly darker and draw a visible B/C line. WCAG asks 3:1 for graphics that are needed to use a control.

Suggested direction

Black-key rows at least 1.6–2:1 against white-key rows, a brighter octave (B/C) line, beat lines at least 1.5:1 and bar lines at least 3:1. Re-measure across all 13 themes.

Code: ui/src/ui/theme.ts:45, ui/src/views/roll/grid.ts

U5 High Global Measured

Default type and hit targets are very small at 100% interface scale

What happens

On the first-run screen (1920 × 1080) 46 of 101 controls use 10 px type and some labels go down to 8 px. PAT/SONG is 38 × 11 px (8.5 px type), Mute/Solo 22 × 19 px, Count-in 39 × 22 px (9 px), the FX-count badge 20 × 18 px (9 px) and CLIP 30 × 14 px (8 px).

Why it is a problem

  • At 100% on a 27″ 1440p monitor a 10 px em is about 2.3 mm tall. Small neighbours like M beside S invite mis-clicks.
  • PAT/SONG is the switch that decides whether Space plays the pattern or the song; at 11 px tall it is easy to miss.
  • The remedy exists (Settings → Look → Interface scale, 80–150%) but it is opt-in and buried.
  • At 150% the interface is comfortable, but on a 1080p screen it then shows 5 tracks with the mixer open, and the toolbar silently drops the metronome, input-monitoring and count-in buttons (still in the View menu).

Suggested direction

Set floors at 100%: 11 px type and 24 px targets; keep FL-style density through spacing rather than type size. Default to 110–125% on high-DPI displays, and expose the scale in the View menu with a visible readout.

Code: ui/src/views/Settings.tsx:327, ui/src/lib/toolbarFit.ts, ui/src/styles.css

U6 Medium Toolbar Reproduced

Update prompt sits on the hint line, and the hint is regularly cut off

What happens

About a second after launch a green “Restart to update” pill appears at a fixed spot on the toolbar’s second row, on top of the contextual hint, cutting it to “…? s…”. Separately, the hint shares a roughly 230 px slot with the status text and is often ellipsized (“Whole song in view · 40 bars Draw: click inserts · drag moves · edges tri…”), which also makes the “? shortcuts” link inside it unreachable.

Why it is a problem

  • The hint line is the app’s main inline help and a first-class setting (“Hints: what the current tool does”). It is also where some modes are explained, e.g. “SONG mode — Space plays the song from the playlist”.
  • It shows whenever an update is available, in other words for every user of an outdated build, at every window size.

Suggested direction

Give updates a slot of their own (end of the menu row, or the status area as “Update available”), and let the hint own the rest of the row, with a tooltip on truncation.

Code: ui/src/views/Toolbar.tsx, ui/src/views/Updates.tsx

U7 Medium Channel rack Reproduced

“Add channel” is a 953 px column that hides instruments on laptop screens

What happens

“+ Channel” opens one vertical menu with 35+ entries in four groups (Sampler › 12 categories, Synthesizer › 11, Sampled instruments, Plugin instruments). At 1920 × 1080 it is 953 px tall and opens upward from a 79 × 20 px button, covering the menubar and transport. At 1366 × 768 it becomes a scroll area (953 px of content in 760 px) with no scrollbar or fade: the list visibly ends at “Synkopa Keys — grand piano”.

Why it is a problem

  • The main “add an instrument” entry point is slow: hover a group, hover a category, scroll.
  • On a common laptop resolution Music Box and every VST3 instrument are below the fold with nothing to say they exist.

Suggested direction

Reuse the effect picker pattern that already works well (search box, categories with counts, tiles with descriptions), or a multi-column menu that fits.

Code: ui/src/views/ChannelRack.tsx, ui/src/views/patternShared.tsx

U8 Medium Dialogs Reproduced

Modal dialogs do not keep keyboard focus; Esc then stops closing them

What happens

In the Welcome dialog and in the “Unsaved changes” prompt, Tab moves focus out to the menubar behind the modal (the focus ring lands on “File”). A/B on the prompt: Esc closes it while focus is inside; after two Tabs, neither one nor two Escapes close it.

Why it is a problem

  • This breaks the standard modal contract: keyboard and screen-reader users can tab into controls they cannot see.
  • Esc stops working on the very dialog that guards unsaved work, forcing a switch to the mouse.

Suggested direction

Trap focus in every modal and handle Esc on the overlay rather than on the focused element.

Code: ui/src/ui/Confirm.tsx, ui/src/views/Updates.tsx (welcome)

U9 Medium Channel rack Reproduced

Channel settings opens on top of the Channel rack

What happens

Clicking a channel name opens its settings window centred over the rack, hiding the channel rows and the step grid.

Why it is a problem

  • The two are used together: tune the sound while auditioning steps.
  • From a fresh layout the window has to be dragged aside every time it is opened.

Suggested direction

Open it offset to the side of the rack (cascaded, as FL does for plugin windows), or remember its position relative to the rack.

Code: ui/src/views/ChannelWindow.tsx, ui/src/state/docking.ts

U10 Medium Piano roll Reproduced

Three time notations for the same kind of value

What happens

The ruler writes “1.2” (bar.beat) and “1.2.3” (bar.beat.16th). The note properties popup writes Start as “1:1:1” (colons) and Length as “2” (unitless steps). The toolbar says “new note: 1/8” and the transport “1:01:01”.

Why it is a problem

  • The ruler and the properties popup are on screen at the same time, so the same moment is shown in two notations that the user has to translate.
  • “2” gives no unit: steps, beats or seconds.

Suggested direction

One notation everywhere (the transport’s bar:beat:16th) and a unit on lengths (“2 steps · 1/8”).

Code: ui/src/ui/timeRuler.ts:26, ui/src/views/roll (note properties)

U11 Medium Mixer and track headers Measured

Unlabelled controls and names that do not fit

What happens

Each mixer strip has two 30 × 30 px knobs with no label; only the right one shows a value (“128%”, “mono”) and it is the stereo width. Each track header has an unlabelled thin volume slider under the name. The demo project’s own names truncate at default widths: “Pad Cinematic 11…”, and in the mixer “Ghost …”, “Glide L…”, “808 C…” and “→ Synths Bus · Space …”. The knobs are plain divs: not focusable, with no role.

Why it is a problem

  • “128%” under an unlabelled knob could be volume, pan or a send. The only explanation is a delayed native tooltip.
  • Long, descriptive names are the norm for samples and presets, so this is everyday data, not an edge case.

Suggested direction

Label the knobs (PAN / WIDTH) or put the label in the value line (“Width 128%”); allow wider strips or two-line names; make the title the full name; make knobs focusable with arrow keys.

Code: ui/src/views/Mixer.tsx, ui/src/views/Playlist.tsx (lane header)

U12 Medium Help and tooltips Real-app check pending

All help text lives in native title tooltips

What happens

About 360 controls carry a native title attribute and there is no tooltip component. The strings are long: the channel button’s tooltip is about 200 characters with five click variants, and the “Keyboard shortcuts” link carries a 20-line, 900-character tooltip.

Why it is a problem

  • Tooltips are the only labelling for dozens of icon-only controls.
  • Native tooltips appear after about a second, use the small system font, have no key styling and vanish when the pointer moves. A paragraph in that format is hard to read, and help that is hard to read is not used.
Channel button (≈200 chars):
Kick · sampler · kick-808-short.flac — click = channel settings · F7 = Piano roll · Ctrl+click = preview
· Shift+click = select several (Shift+Ctrl+click = one more / less) · right-click = menu

“Keyboard shortcuts” link (first 3 of 20 lines):
Ctrl+drag = select box · Ctrl+click a note = toggle · Ctrl+click a key = every note of that pitch · Shift+I = invert selection · Ctrl+A = all
Shift+drag a note = clone · while moving, press Shift = time only, Ctrl = pitch only · hold Alt = no grid
Double-click a note = properties · Alt+wheel on a note = velocity 5 % (Ctrl+Alt = 1 %)

Suggested direction

A styled tooltip (first line = name, keycaps for shortcuts, details below) and feed the existing hint line on hover.

Code: ui/src (≈360 title attributes), ui/src/views/Toolbar.tsx (hint line)

U13 Medium Help Reproduced

Keyboard shortcuts help is one flat list with no search and duplicate rows

What happens

Help → Keyboard shortcuts opens a two-column list of about 150 rows in a 2073 px scroll area. There is no search and no category headers. “Deselect — Esc” and “Deselect — Ctrl D” appear as two separate rows.

Why it is a problem

  • Finding one shortcut means scrolling more than two screens of same-weight rows.
  • The command palette (Ctrl+K) already has a searchable list of the same commands.

Suggested direction

Add a search box and category headers, generated from the same command list as the palette.

What happens

Typing “dock” lists “Dock left”, “Dock right” and “Dock at the bottom” three times each, once per dockable pane, with no pane name on any of them.

U15 Low Settings Reproduced

Settings: content below the fold with no cue, scroll carried between tabs, and an action that is not a setting

What happens

At 1080p the General page needs 813 px and the Look page 1020 px inside a 610 px pane; Recording (metronome, count-in) and “Restore defaults” are below the fold with no visible scrollbar. The scroll position carries over when switching tabs. “Open demo project”, which replaces the open project, sits in General between Autosave and Editing.

Why it is a problem

  • Options that are not seen are not set. Recording options are exactly what a new user looks for.
  • A destructive action inside a settings page is where nobody expects it.

Suggested direction

Size the dialog to the content or show a persistent scroll affordance; reset scroll on tab change; move “Open demo project” to File → New project (templates).

Code: ui/src/views/Settings.tsx

U16 Low Help menu Reproduced

Help menu has no About, manual or documentation link

What happens

Help offers Ask AI, Find a command, Keyboard shortcuts, Check for updates, What’s new and Join the Discord. The version lives in Settings → Updates. There is no user manual or docs link.

Why it is a problem

  • “What version am I on?” and “where is the manual?” are the two most common reasons people open Help.

Suggested direction

Add “About Synkopa” (version, build, licences, links) and a “Documentation” entry.

U17 Low Piano roll Reproduced

Piano roll opens maximised and hides the Playlist, Mixer and Browser

What happens

F7 opens the Piano roll covering the whole workspace. “Restore the window size” is a 24 px icon in its title bar.

Why it is a problem

  • Switching between editing a pattern and seeing the arrangement costs a click each way, and the restore control is not obvious.

Suggested direction

Open as a large window (e.g. 60% of the height) by default and let users save a maximised layout.

U18 Low Mixer Reproduced

“Route 1 selected here” reads as a label, not as a control

What happens

The Mixer’s title bar shows “Route 1 selected here Ctrl L”. It is a button: “Channel rack channels selected: 1 · Ctrl+L routes them to the selected insert · Shift+Ctrl+L spreads them over the inserts from it on”.

Why it is a problem

  • It is the only place the current routing source is shown, and nothing about its look says it can be clicked.

U20 Low Piano roll › Tools Reproduced

Tools panel: Seed field looks empty or disabled; jitter values have no unit

What happens

In the Tools panel the Seed input renders as an empty dark box with no value, placeholder or hint. “Timing jitter 0.30” and “Velocity jitter 0.20” show bare numbers.

Why it is a problem

  • An empty dark box next to two active sliders looks disabled, and the user cannot tell whether a seed is set.

U21 Low First run Real-app check pending

A new project opens onto an empty Playlist with no on-canvas guidance

What happens

File → New project (and “Start empty” on first run) opens an empty Playlist with thirty tracks named “Track 1…30” and the Channel rack on top. The only help is the hint line, which describes the current tool.

Why it is a problem

  • The next step (paint a pattern with B, or drag one from the Browser) is not suggested anywhere in the view.
  • To confirm in the real app: the mock boots with a starter sketch, so the real first-run project may differ.

Suggested direction

A short dismissible hint in the empty Playlist (“Pick a pattern on the left and paint it here with B”), and number tracks only as they are used.

What already works well

Effect picker

Search, categories with counts, plain-language descriptions, preset panel and keyboard hints. The best surface in the app, and the pattern U7 asks to reuse.

Export dialog

Compact and complete: Mix/Stems, Pattern/Song, tail, format, bit depth, sample rate, plus a duration and file-size estimate before committing.

Unsaved-changes prompt

Specific wording (“Save before creating a new project?”), safe default focus on Save, destructive choice in red. Only its focus handling needs work (U8).

Plugin editors

Clear sections, labelled knobs, a response curve, and ‹ › to move through the chain.

Status readouts and record feedback

The readout explains what is under the pointer (“2 clips are stacked here”, “Beat Low-Pass Filter · 120 Hz · 15%”) and what Record will do (“Record armed: Space records to Vocal after a bar of count-in”).

Consistent FL-style keymap and window keys

F5–F9, Ctrl+L routing, Ctrl+B duplicate, a shared ruler with the same gestures in every editor, and Esc closes the top window.

Scale, themes and responsive toolbar

Interface scale 80–150%, 13 themes with previews, and a measured 12-level toolbar fit that keeps the bar on one row at any width.

Method, scope and limits

How. The UI mock build (the same front-end code with an in-browser backend) was driven with trusted input events in headless Chromium through scripted journeys: first run, new project, programming steps, drawing notes, placing and editing clips, routing and effects, export, settings and help. Measurements come from computed styles and canvas pixels, and every number in this report was read that way rather than estimated from a screenshot. Each scripted step was checked against the engine’s state, not the pixels.

What the mock cannot show. Real audio, native file dialogs, plugin scanning, native tooltips and the true first-run project. Those are marked “Real-app check pending” (U12, U21) and are the subject of a short pass in the installed app.

Not covered. Recording with real inputs, latency and audio quality, MIDI hardware, VST plugin windows of third-party plugins, save/open via native dialogs, very large projects, the Polish UI and the light themes (spot-checked only).

FL conventions that are deliberate, not findings. The project’s stated default is FL Studio behaviour. Right-click to delete, Ctrl+N for “Save new version”, Esc closing the top window, the Playlist switching the transport to SONG mode, and the greyed bar that extends a pattern are all FL parity. U1 and U2 keep those gestures and ask only for a safer target and for feedback.

Reproduce. Capture rig, scripts and all screenshots are in /home/reneb/_mycode/synkopa-ux-review (driver/, shots/, findings-log.md).
